title: Charisma
identity: Paul Ballam-Cross’s Charisma is an unaccompanied saxophone work; Wirripang offers separate alto, tenor and soprano editions. The composer’s current compositions page gives a five-minute solo work, while the tenor edition page gives approximately three minutes, three movements, composition 2013/revision 2014, lyrical character and indie-rock/dance influences. Version-specific timing remains unresolved.

evidence.claim: Lists solo soprano/alto/tenor saxophone Charisma, five minutes.
Tenor edition is solo, about three minutes, three movements; lyrical, influenced by indie rock/dance artists; composed 2013, revised 2014; score sample download available.

Wirripang’s one-page sample is an alto saxophone solo marked “written for Emma Di Marco.” It shows three movements: I “Out of Focus” marked Fast, rubato; II “Pulse” marked Slow (quarter note=50); and III “Skyline, 2 A.M.” marked Presto (quarter note=150). The sample uses a single treble-clef line with frequent chromatic accidentals, varied slurred and separated note groups, and broad printed dynamic changes. These are observations from the alto sample only.
evidence.source_name: Wirripang public score sample for Charisma

score_observations: In the inspected one-page alto-saxophone sample, movement I opens with a rapid rubato line marked fff, followed by descending chromatic gestures and softer quasi-echo phrases. Movement II begins slowly at quarter note=50 with a sustained lyrical line and crescendos, then rises into a high register. Movement III is marked Presto at quarter note=150 and uses repeated rhythmic figures with chromatic motion and changing dynamics. No exact pitch range is asserted.
review_focus: Inference from the inspected alto sample: assess control of the movement-specific tempo shifts, rubato, chromatic runs, register changes, and broad dynamic contrasts. The sample is not the tenor edition, so do not transfer these details automatically.
